content:
incident-bot: Pager — SEV1: potential cross-tenant data exposure detected in dedicated pool eu-central-1 (pool: dedicated-eu-central1). Affected customer: NovaMed (VPC). Initial alert: anomaly-detector flagged overlapping session prefixes and mismatched response tenant_id. Ticket: INC-2026-498. Pager routed to oncall.

rachel_ops: Ack. I'm oncall and taking lead. Joining packet captures and router state now. Please avoid sharing raw patient IDs here.

tom_sre: I see router entries where the same source 10.50.22.9 returned two different tenant_id headers within 90s. Snippet from router audit (sanitized):
```
TS=21:40:02 src=10.50.22.9 tenant_header=nm-100 response_tenant=nm-100
TS=21:40:54 src=10.50.22.9 tenant_header=nm-100 response_tenant=nm-201
```

dana_cs: NovaMed reports "patient record 0x7a9 mixed with 0x3de" in their app UI. They have paused writes and set app to read-only. Legal is on call.

security_mgr: SOC: preserve all evidence. Creating SOC-2026-90, do not rotate logs or redact until we snapshot.

rachel_ops: Immediate mitigation applied: isolated dedicated-eu-central1 from shared-route-gateway and set pool into tenant-lock mode. Commands executed:
```
routefix isolate --pool dedicated-eu-central1 --mode tenant-lock
netctl detach-gateway --pool dedicated-eu-central1 --gateway shared-route-gw-2
```

deploy-bot: Deploy started: router daemon patch (kv-cache TTL fix) to g5,g6 (canary 5%). Build: rb-kvfix-1.2.0.

vikas: Noted. I'm running a quick verification script to enumerate active prefix bindings vs. kv-cache snapshot.

vikas: Verification output (sanitized):
```
active_bindings: [nm-100, nm-201]
kv_cache_snapshot: {prefix:10.50.22, tenant:nm-100, ttl: 3s, last_refresh: 21:39:20}
stale_entries: [prefix:10.50.22 -> tenant:nm-100 (stale)]
```

tom_sre: Root cause hypothesis: during a control-plane rolling update earlier today, a race allowed a stale kv_cache entry to be reused for a new session bound to a different tenant_id. The TTL calc and refresh hook didn't run under reconnect. Repro steps noted locally.

dana_cs: NovaMed asks for ETA to full remediation and whether any PHI was exfiltrated. We told them we will provide a timeline and will follow with a formal customer letter after SOC + Legal review.

security_mgr: Immediate customer notification template sent to Legal for review. Legal joined thread: @legal please advise on disclosure obligations and next steps.

legal: Reviewing incident. Requesting precise list of affected records (counts only), window of exposure, and mitigation steps taken. Do not share patient identifiers in slack.

rachel_ops: Mitigation progress: forced kv-cache eviction across pool and pinned route map to tenant binding. Commands: `kvctl evict --pool dedicated-eu-central1 --force` and `routectl pin --pool dedicated-eu-central1 --enforce-tenant-bindings`. Also kicked active connections to force reconnect.

deploy-bot: Canary passed: rb-kvfix-1.2.0 on g5,g6. Rolling to remaining nodes g7,g8 now.

vikas: Post-mitigation sampling shows no mixed-tenant responses in router logs for 15m. Sample sanitized log:
```
21:57:12 src=10.50.22.9 tenant=nm-100 route_hash=0xb12a
21:57:18 src=10.50.23.4 tenant=nm-201 route_hash=0xc92f
```

dana_cs: NovaMed acknowledged mitigation and resumed limited reads. They requested a post-incident call after initial SOC review.

security_mgr: SOC snapshot collected: router config, kv-cache dumps, pcap, and timeline. SOC-2026-90 updated. No evidence yet of remote exfiltration, but still under analysis.

tom_sre: Action items for postmortem: 1) Fix kv-cache TTL and add jitter on refresh (tom_sre) 2) Add E2E reconnect tests with tenant churn (eng-qa) 3) Harden control-plane rolling upgrade sequence to prevent transient stale bindings (eng-platform)

rachel_ops: Customer comms owner: dana_cs (prepare timeline and customer-facing memo). Postmortem owners assigned as above. I'm creating runbook addendum: emergency `routefix isolate` + `kvctl evict` steps.

deploy-bot: Full rollout completed: rb-kvfix-1.2.0 -> g5,g6,g7,g8. Monitoring for 30m.

vikas: Handoff: I'll stay until the 30m monitor completes then hand to night oncall @tom_sre. Leaving a concise runbook in INC-2026-498.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: SEV1 -> Mitigated (mitigations: pool isolation, kv-cache eviction, router daemon patch). Please ensure INC-2026-498 is updated with SOC ticket SOC-2026-90 and Legal notes. Last confirmed suspicious event timestamp: 1899991283.

legal: We will coordinate the notification letter with CS after SOC completes scope. Schedule a review within 48h.

rachel_ops: Closing active pager now. If SOC finds any new leads, reopen. Thanks team.
